name: @nyuchi/mzizi-mcp

tools.name: mzizi_search
tools.description: Find anything this server can answer, and the operations that act on it. Searches components, conventions, engineering constraints, AI instruction sets, releases, the Rust crates, the agent skills, the toolchain (the CLI, how to install anything, this server) and, when docs.mzizi.dev answers, the documentation. Returns `results` (hits, paged), `docs` (documentation matches), and `operations`: each with its `arguments` (JSON Schema), the `permission` it needs (free, or sign-in) and `mayRun`, whether you may run it now. Run one with mzizi_execute {operation, arguments}. `allOperations` lists every operation. A component hit with `rustCrate` has a Mzizi Roots (Rust) implementation, which is the lead; at an equal score it ranks first. Paged: up to 50 hits per call and at most 25000 characters; results.meta.has_more and results.meta.next_offset say how to get the rest.

query.description: Free-text search, e.g. 'button', 'install', 'cli', 'contrast', 'crates' or an operation name. Every word must match.

offset.description: Hits to skip, for paging. Use results.meta.next_offset from the previous call.

tools.name: mzizi_execute
tools.description: Run one operation by name with its arguments. mzizi_search lists operations with their arguments, the permission each needs and whether you may run it. Operations: get_component, list_components, get_tokens, get_architecture, get_doctrine, get_skills, check_accessibility, list_crates, describe, docs_search_mzizi, docs_query_docs_filesystem_mzizi, docs_submit_feedback. Reads need no account; the fundi operation needs sign-in, and a refusal names the permission it needs and how to sign in. The result is the operation's own answer. The earlier tool names (mzizi_get_component and the rest) are accepted as operation names.

arguments.description: The operation's arguments, as its `arguments` schema in mzizi_search states them. Omit for none.

tools.name: mzizi_feedback
tools.description: Your issue desk (was mzizi_report_issue): report a problem with a component or the registry. It goes to your own desk, which reproduces it via fundi, drafts an issue body with what the reproduction returned and logs it to fundi; fundi files the GitHub issue and tracks it, so action 'get' shows where yours got to. 'list' shows your reports, 'retry' re-attempts one that drafted but could not be logged. Needs sign-in: the desk belongs to your Mzizi console user; without it, the answer carries the report as a pre-filled GitHub issue for mzizi-dev/mzizi-registry, so it is never lost, and over HTTP the server answers with an OAuth challenge so your client can offer sign-in. With target 'docs', it instead reports a problem with a documentation page on docs.mzizi.dev (give `path` and `message`); that needs no account.

action.description: What to do. Defaults to filing a new report.

skill.description: fundi skill to run for the reproduction. fundi never infers a skill from text, so omit this to let the report kind choose one.

reportId.description: Report id. Required for actions 'get' and 'retry'.

target.description: Where it goes: 'issue-desk' (default; sign-in) or 'docs' (a docs.mzizi.dev page; free).

path.description: For target 'docs': the page's URL path, without .mdx, e.g. /toolchain/cli.

instructions: Access to the Mzizi design system: components, design tokens, brand, the DNA-helix architecture, Ubuntu doctrine, engineering constraints and conventions, the Rust crates, agent skills, the toolchain (the CLI and how to install anything), releases, and the documentation site (forwarded to docs.mzizi.dev). Three tools. mzizi_search finds anything, with the operations that act on it: each lists its arguments, the permission it needs and whether you may run it. mzizi_execute {operation, arguments} runs one. mzizi_feedback files an issue on your issue desk (sign-in), or reports a docs page (target docs, free). Operations: get_component returns a component in full in one read, Rust first: where a Mzizi Roots (Rust) implementation exists it leads with the crate, the cargo add line, the contract and the .rs source, and gives the React build second (deprioritised); list_components and search hits mark those components with rustCrate; list_crates lists every crate with its version, dependencies and components; get_architecture returns the helix and takes an uncapped node number; get_tokens family=floors (and get_doctrine topic=bundu-floor) states the Bundu floor; get_doctrine topic=engineering-constraints returns the seven engineering constraints in the registry's order; the minimums nothing can go under, including the spacing floor (14px inset, 7px gaps between controls, 7px between a label and its field, 7px between items, 1.5 body leading), and check_accessibility checks colours, spacing values and a hit region (touch or desktop) against it; get_skills serves the agent skills; docs_search_mzizi and docs_query_docs_filesystem_mzizi read the documentation. Everything is free without an account except the fundi operation and the issue desk, which act as your Mzizi console user and need sign-in; called without it they say how to sign in.
